title: Renaissance Art and the Masters
text: The Renaissance (roughly 14th–17th centuries) witnessed a flourishing of art in Europe, particularly in Italy, characterized by realistic depiction of human figures, use of perspective, and a return to classical themes. Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa and The Last Supper remain among the most recognized paintings in the world. Michelangelo created the ceiling frescoes of the Sistine Chapel (1508–1512) and the sculpture David (1501–1504). Raphael was known for his Madonnas and the School of Athens fresco. These artists studied anatomy, geometry, and classical antiquity to achieve unprecedented realism. The Renaissance broke from the flat, symbolic style of medieval art and established conventions that dominated Western art for centuries.
